sn48.58:1.1: This is famously the scene of Sāriputta’s awakening ([mn74:1.2]()).
sn48.58:1.3: The interpretation of this discourse is problematic. However, I believe it is thematically similar to [sn16.5](), where Mahākassapa explains that he continues his austere lifestyle even though he is enlightened both because he enjoys it, and to inspire future generations. The current text seems corrupt, and no parallels are recorded. | I take the expression _pavattamāno pavattati_ (“in rolling forth, roll forth”) as referring to Sāriputta’s role as the disciple who, like no other, continues to “roll forth” the wheel of the teaching ([mn111:23.1](), [sn8.7:3.4](), [an1.187:1.1]()). The Buddha is asking what motivates Sāriputta to teach.
sn48.58:1.4: Presumably this means so that others can realize awakening.
sn48.58:2.1: text seems corrupt, the indriyas are not enlightenment …
sn48.58:3.2: Five things leading to non-decline of the dispensation.
